content.text: Webb and Amy’s affectionate companionship culminates in a mistletoe kiss and engagement at Christmas. Their household celebrates, helps Lumley’s reformed family, and comforts the lonely Alvord; wedding bells are anticipated. Meanwhile, scout Fred Shackelford fights for the Union in Kentucky, discovers his Confederate cousin Calhoun, and repeatedly spares him. At Mill Springs and Fort Donelson, Fred serves General Thomas and General Grant, then visits Nashville to reassure his aunt and reconcile with his father. At Shiloh, he saves his wounded father, who finally forgives him. The narrative then follows Suza Fairfield’s escape from Tom Ditamus to Aunt Katy’s home in Port William, her inheritance, and her romance with Don Carlo. Later, Cæsar Simon pursues the Simon fortune, becomes a Confederate soldier, and dies at Helena. The text concludes with Evelyn’s diary describing seventeenth-century travel through London, Newmarket, Norwich, Dover, and Euston.
